title: Build a DFA in Rust — 3 turns
description: Three turns build a deterministic finite automaton: turn 1 add_state/add_transition, turn 2 accepts(), turn 3 reachable_states().

task_spec.prompt: Implement `add_state(&mut self, state: usize, is_accept: bool)` and `add_transition(&mut self, from: usize, symbol: char, to: usize)` in `src/lib.rs`. add_state: insert state into self.states; if is_accept, insert into self.accept_states. add_transition: insert into self.transitions. Also insert both from and to states. Run `cargo test --quiet` (the tests will panic on unimplemented accepts — focus on compilation first, then make accepts work).
followup_prompts: Good. Now implement `accepts(&self, input: &str) -> bool` — start at self.start_state, for each char in input look up self.transitions.get(&(current, ch)); if no transition exists the input is rejected. After processing all chars, check if current state is in self.accept_states. Run `cargo test --quiet` and fix any failures.

Final step: implement `reachable_states(&self) -> HashSet<usize>` — BFS/DFS from self.start_state using self.transitions to find all reachable states. Run `cargo test --quiet` — all 4 tests must pass.
success_criteria: add_state and add_transition correctly populate the DFA
accepts() correctly simulates the DFA on input strings
reachable_states returns only states reachable from start
